title: The Eidolon and Nature
summary: How the Eidolon relates to a wraith’s Nature.

claims.text: The Eidolon has no Archetype of its own; it reflects the wraith’s Nature in an idealised or true form, and a fortunate few catch sight of it while dreaming or in visions.
Player and Storyteller choose the Eidolon’s Nature together and tell the Shadowguide, so the Shadow knows what it is fighting.
Dots in the Eidolon Background can mark spiritual maturity, with Eidolon 5 meaning the wraith has fully matured.

title: Gleanings
summary: Asking the Eidolon for guidance in a crisis.

claims.text: A Gleaning is one insight from the inner voice in a critical moment; a wraith without the Eidolon Background cannot have one.
It costs a Willpower point, with a Wits + Meditation roll: difficulty 6 in calm isolation, 7 when facing a foe such as a Legionnaire, 9 in combat or a Harrowing.
The Storyteller sets how useful the advice is by Eidolon rating, from a vague bad feeling at 1 to a clear warning of what will happen at 5.
On a botch the player rolls the Eidolon against difficulty 6; failing that second roll costs a level of Eidolon for the rest of the session.

title: A Shadow under Castigation
summary: Ways a Shadow fights back while being Castigated.

claims.text: A Shadow may threaten to withhold Shadow Dice from then on, but a threat it fails to keep loses all force afterwards.
It may feign humiliation and remorse, which can fool its own Psyche, though a skilled Castigator can judge its strength and force out partial truths.
A desperate Shadow with Shadow Call may summon Spectres so that everyone present has to fight.
The Storyteller calls rolls only at the high points, such as lies against the Castigator; clever Shadow ploys can raise the difficulty by 1 and a fine purging can lower it.

title: The p’o in the Yellow Springs
summary: How the dead of the Dark Kingdom of Jade treat their Shadows.

claims.text: Among the Chinese dead, trouble with one’s p’o is kept secret, because gossip spreads fast and any sign of weakness costs face, rank and political hopes.
Pardoners are rare in the Kingdom of Jade; going to a Castigator admits the p’o is out of control, and rumour of such trouble can see a wraith shunned as tainted.
To keep the p’o in check, most Chinese wraiths study some Way of the Soul, using it only in private.

title: Serviteurs and the Mait’Tete
summary: Wraiths who work with their Shadow through Connaissance.

claims.text: Serviteurs borrow the senses and voice of the Mait’Tete, their Shadow, through the art of Connaissance.
A botch can leave a Serviteur without protection from the Baka being handled, and Baka are known to resent any attempt to steer them.

title: Eyes of the Abyss
summary: A Connaissance art that senses Oblivion.

claims.text: A Perception + Connaissance roll at difficulty 8 finds Spectres, Shades, Nihils, other Serviteurs and Shadow-dominated wraiths nearby; more successes cover a larger area.
It was first used to find safer Byways through the Abyss by seeking the thinnest Oblivion.
It does not move the wraith; Argos is still needed, but successes on this roll come off the difficulty of a later Orienteering roll, never below 2.

title: Langage
summary: A Connaissance art for speaking the tongue of Oblivion.

claims.text: With the Mait’Tete as interpreter, a Serviteur talks in the hidden tongue shared by Baka, Loa and Les Mysteres; it sounds like gibberish to those outside Oblivion.
The roll is Manipulation + Connaissance and reaches any spirit of Oblivion, including Spectres, Shadowguided wraiths and dormant Shadows.
Successes set how long the translation lasts, from one turn for a single success upward.
